description:
Bug in src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr handle_error (lines ~398-475):

  Every handler wraps its inner error in DNSError, regardless of the
  original cause. This makes the exception type useless for callers
  that want to distinguish failure modes.

  Current mapping:
    URI::Error       -> DNSError  (wrong: parse error, not DNS)
    Socket::Error    -> DNSError  (correct in spirit)
    IO::TimeoutError -> TimeoutError (correct)
    OpenSSL::SSL::Error -> DNSError (wrong: SSL, not DNS)
    Crest::RequestFailed -> HTTPClientError or HTTPServerError (correct)
    other           -> FetchError (correct)

  The inner Error object does carry the right type (Error.invalid_url,
  Error.dns), but the wrapper exception's *class* is DNSError, which
  is what callers rescue on.

Repro:

  begin
    client.get(\"http://not a valid url/\")
  rescue ex : Fetcher::DNSError
    # This catches even though the cause was a URI parse error.
  end

  Callers who want to retry on transient DNS failures will retry on
  bad URL parse errors too.

Fix:

  In each handler, raise the exception type that matches the *cause*:

    handle_uri_error    -> InvalidURLError
    handle_socket_error -> DNSError (keep)
    handle_timeout_error -> TimeoutError (keep)
    handle_ssl_error    -> SSLError (new) or DNSError with internal marker
    handle_request_failed -> HTTPError subclass (keep)
    handle_unknown_error -> FetchError (keep)

  Or, more conservatively, keep DNSError but add a #cause_type getter
  on FetchError that returns the inner Error's type, and document the
  convention.

  Recommend the first (correct exception types) since the existing
  exceptions.cr already has InvalidURLError, TimeoutError, and the
  HTTPError family.

Test: spec/crest_http_client_error_handling_spec.cr (5KB) should gain
assertions like `expect_raises(Fetcher::InvalidURLError)` for the URI
parse case.
title: Stop using DNSError as the universal catch-all wrapper
